invalidated_v1_reason: S6 v1 used a permanent shared_materialized_keys set instead of per-tier physical residency. It undercounted refcount-zero resident hits and skipped causal recopy after tier eviction.
question: With stable shared-prefix content identity and exact per-tier physical lifetimes, how do reuse, eviction, rematerialization, recovery, copy amplification, and HBM/DRAM occupancy change?
selection_policy: All 60 registered cells and all three seeds are retained regardless of WCT direction, hit-rate shape, significance, eviction/rematerialization count, or whether AegisKV improves any metric.

hardware.gpu: NVIDIA A100 40GB modeled as 40 GiB addressable HBM
hardware.placement: one TP1/PP1 replica per GPU in two complete 8-GPU nodes

same_node.peer_rule: bijective successor GPU within each 8-GPU node
same_node.dram_rule: CPU DRAM attached to the source node

cross_node.peer_rule: bijective GPU target on the next node in a node ring
cross_node.dram_rule: CPU DRAM attached to the next node in the ring

capacity_equation.no_oracle: dispatch and prefix admission never inspect realized output length, realized service, or future cohort members

shared_prefix_semantics.content_identity: Within each source rank, requests sorted by (arrival_ms, request_id) are partitioned into consecutive groups of four. Stable logical identity is (group_id, chunk_ordinal).
shared_prefix_semantics.physical_epoch_identity: Each tier uses a generation owner ID (content identity, tier, epoch); the owner ID may change after eviction while content identity remains fixed.
shared_prefix_semantics.tier_state_machine: UNMATERIALIZED -> PENDING -> COMMITTED -> EVICTED. Rejected attempts are immediately finalized and remain only in immutable epoch audit lineage.
shared_prefix_semantics.same_tier_duplicate_rule: PENDING or COMMITTED suppresses another physical copy in that tier.
shared_prefix_semantics.independent_tier_rule: HBM and DRAM are evaluated independently. A surviving PENDING/COMMITTED tier never prevents causal readmission of a missing other tier.
shared_prefix_semantics.resident_cache_rule: A COMMITTED object is a resident alias hit even at logical refcount zero; active-overlap and resident hits are reported separately.
shared_prefix_semantics.eviction_rule: On a later source seal, an EVICTED epoch is finalized before a new epoch attempts admission. Rejected and replaced epochs leave active/controller/baseline registries.
shared_prefix_semantics.aggregate_priority_rule: For each stable content chunk, every live tier epoch uses the minimum predicted residual-DAG slack among currently active logical members. At refcount zero, slack is set to the full chunk recompute cost, making current protection benefit zero. A later active alias refreshes slack metadata. update_slack must not copy, evict, or change used bytes.
shared_prefix_semantics.recovery: Recovery reads only a continuous chain of the selected tier's current COMMITTED epochs; PENDING, rejected, finalized, or evicted epochs contribute zero.
shared_prefix_semantics.legacy_observed_content_set: shared_materialized_keys is retained only as an ever-admitted logical-content set and never controls copy or recovery. A key is added only after at least one tier admits an epoch.

sweep.gate_cells: reuse={0,1} x same_node x 2 policies x first seed = 4

workload.probe_schedule: equal-width stratified timestamps over the common 90 s arrival window; identical probe tuples across all reuse, topology, and policy cells for a seed
workload.primary_denominator: all workflows from one immutable workflow universe per seed; policies share exact request IDs, prefix assignments, and probes

statistics.interval: Student-t 95% confidence interval across seed-level metrics, df=2
primary: request recovery hit and prefix-token/recoverable-byte fraction
HBM and DRAM byte-ms occupancy integral and time-mean GiB per GPU
per-tier epoch admission, rejection, eviction, rematerialization, and no-duplicate counts
active-overlap hit, resident hit, refcount-zero resident hit, and refcount conservation
forbidden_gates: recovery hit must be monotone in reuse
copy amplification must be monotone in reuse
any seed or cell may be removed for curve shape

figure_grammar.layout: 2x3 mechanism panels matching S6 v1 axes, but sourced only from v2 cells
figure_grammar.panel_text_boundary: no pilot, preliminary, seed, hash, or evidence-boundary prose inside the panel

hard_gates: exactly 4 gate cells pass before the full 60-cell run starts
exactly 60 registered cells are atomically published
workflow/probe/assignment hashes match across paired treatments
same-tier PENDING and COMMITTED states schedule no duplicate physical copy
refcount-zero COMMITTED cache is a resident hit
single-tier and full-tier eviction allow independent causal rematerialization
single surviving COMMITTED tier remains recoverable
rejected fresh epochs and replaced evicted epochs leave no orphan active/controller/baseline request
live shared epoch owners equal current PENDING/COMMITTED tier mappings
shared aggregate priority follows visible residual-DAG members; idle demotion and active reactivation are metadata-only with zero copy/used/eviction delta
empty replay is exact and fault replay never lowers WCT
no performance-direction threshold and no seed/cell selection
single-page vector PDF, PNG width >=1800, extracted font >=7 pt
evidence_boundary: Three-seed metadata DES mechanism pilot. A100 capacity/model bytes are frozen, but service coefficients, directional bandwidth, 500 ms Aegis activation, and 60 s Native replacement are modeled/unmeasured. Native Mooncake is a modeled Router+Store approximation. Shared-prefix identity/epochs are experiment-layer metadata, not a verified production Mooncake cache implementation. Not physical A100 or paper-ready evidence.
